messages.subject: Define higher order factor model
parts:
I have the following fou factor model, which gave a very good fit:
model <-'a =~x1+x2+x3
     b=~x4+x5+x6
     c=~x7+x8+x9
     d=~x10+x11+x12'
cfa(model, data=xxx,estimator = "MLM",std.lv=TRUE)

When I defined the one factor model

model <-'a =~x1+x2+x3 + x4+x5+x6 + x7+x8+x9 + x10+x11+x12'
cfa(model, data=xxx,estimator = "MLM",std.lv=TRUE)

thi also gave a good fit, Then I tried 

model <-'a =~x1+x2+x3
     b=~x4+x5+x6
     c=~x7+x8+x9
     d=~x10+x11+x12
     High =~ a+b+c+d'
cfa(model, data=xxx,estimator = "MLM",std.lv=TRUE)

I got the message:
In lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
  lavaan WARNING: the optimizer warns that a solution has NOT been found!

What can be the underlying reason for this?

(I also tried with the model:
model <-'a =~x1+x2+x3
     b=~x4+x5+x6
     c=~x7+x8+x9
     d=~x10+x11+x12
     High =~x1+x2+x3 + x4+x5+x6 + x7+x8+x9 + x10+x11+x12'
which resulted in:
1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel2, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could
    not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not
    identified.
2: In lav_test_satorra_bentler(lavobject = NULL, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not invert information matrix needed for robust test statistic

Thanks

Judit

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Define higher order factor model
parts:
With common factors standardized, the solution is indeterminate with respect to sign. Supply a starting value for one loading somewhere, which you might do via:

  High =~ start(1)*a+b+c+d  

and that might resolve the issue. There are two solutions for the model, and it can't seem to decide between them. Perhaps your sample size is also low, leading to high uncertainty for the algorithm.

For your bifactor model, where observed variables load on both a, b, c, d and on High, you must specify that High is uncorrelated with a, b, c, d. Otherwise, there is likely to be no solution.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Define higher order factor model
parts:
got the same message. 
 Any new suggestion?

Maybe the higher order factor doesn't make sense.  Have you inspected your results of the first-order CFA model?

model <-'a =~x1+x2+x3
     b=~x4+x5+x6
     c=~x7+x8+x9
     d=~x10+x11+x12'
fit <- cfa(model, data=xxx,estimator = "MLM",std.lv=TRUE)
lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv")

That model should already (a) fit well and (b) have a pattern of factor correlations that supports the hypothesis of a common cause before fitting a higher-order factor.
